name: Gas Sensor Drift ML Benchmark
description: Classification, Regression, and Clustering under Sensor Drift Reproducible machine-learning benchmark for the UCI Gas Sensor Array Drift at Different Concentrations dataset (ID 270, DOI: 10.24432/C5MK6M). The benchmark evaluates gas classification, concentration regression, exploratory clustering, feature importance, and computational efficiency under a reproducible and auditable pipeline. It explicitly separates mixed-batch random evaluation from later-batch evaluation, in which models are trained on batches 1–5 and evaluated on batches 6–10. The archived version corresponds to the FULL experimental profile used in the accompanying manuscript. The reported results were generated from experiment commit 5ca408022aa5e44fa286116629553cd44d8e2788. Research questions • RQ1 — How do classical supervised machine-learning models compare for gas classification? • RQ2 — How accurately can gas concentration be estimated from the same sensor representation? • RQ3 — How much does predictive performance degrade when models trained on earlier acquisition batches are evaluated on later batches? • RQ4 — Do unsupervised clusters align more strongly with gas identity or with acquisition batch? • RQ5 — How do predictive performance, training time, inference time, and serialized model size compare across models? Full-profile highlights • Mixed-batch classification reached a macro-F1 of 0.996 with XGBoost.
